LESSON: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are adverts important in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension
2. appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information to a partner. (skill: appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are adverts important in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify adverbs of degree and time in a text for comprehension.
5. Be able to: appreciate reading varied texts to acquire information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
